hints: Look carefully at where each line points: W points to the narrow pinched waist in the middle, X points to the very tip at the end, and Y brackets one whole half of the X-shaped chromosome.
Recall what joins the two halves together in the middle, what caps and protects the ends, and what name we give to one half of a duplicated chromosome.
walkthrough:
**Look at what W, X and Y are actually pointing to**

Look at the micrograph with fresh eyes. Each chromosome is X-shaped because it has already duplicated.

W is the constricted middle where the two halves meet. X is the end tip of an arm. Y is the bracket around the left half of one chromosome.

**Match each position to the correct term**

The constriction that holds the two sister chromatids together is the centromere, so W is the centromere.

The protective cap at the end of a chromosome is the telomere, so X is the telomere. One complete half of the duplicated chromosome is a chromatid, so Y is a chromatid.

**Check why the other words do not fit**

A centriole is a separate organelle that organises the spindle, it is not part of the chromosome itself. A microtubule is a spindle fibre that attaches to the chromosome, it is not the chromatid arm. That leaves only one row that fits all three labels.

options.A: W is not a centriole. A centriole is a cytoplasmic organelle, while W is the waist of the chromosome itself, the centromere.
options.B: W is not a centriole and Y is not a microtubule. Y brackets a whole chromatid arm, not a thin spindle fibre.
options.C: Correct. W is the centromere in the middle, X is the telomere at the tip, and Y is one sister chromatid.
options.D: W and X are correct but Y is wrong. Y shows a thick chromatid, not a thin spindle microtubule.
